# herdr-reviewr [![CI](https://github.com/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr)](https://github.com/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr/releases/latest) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr)](LICENSE)

install · quick start · controls · scopes · configuration · limitations · changelog

A code-review pane for [herdr](https://herdr.dev). Read your agent's diff beside the chat, comment on lines, and send the comments back. ![demo](assets/demo.gif) - **Diff review** — the agent's changes, syntax-highlighted. - **Unified and split views** — one column or side by side, flip with `|`. - **Four diff scopes** — uncommitted, branch, last turn, commits. - **Last-turn diff** — only what the agent's latest turn changed. - **Line comments** — on a line or a range, sent to the agent in one go. - **Text selection** — drag to copy, like an editor. - **File viewer** — any file in the worktree. - **Worktree switch** — follow your agent into another worktree with `W`. - **Search** — files by name and code by content, powered by [fff](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff). - **Find in file** — step through every match. - **PR view** — the branch's pull request, read-only. - **Markdown review** — `m` renders a `.md` file. - **Themes** — 20, dark and light. reviewr never edits your files, never sends on its own, and never posts to your PR. ## Requirements - **herdr ≥ 0.9.3** and **git**. - A terminal with **24-bit color**. - **macOS, Linux, or Windows.** - For the PR tab only: **`gh`**, **`glab`**, or **`az`** (with the `azure-devops` extension), logged in. ## Install ```bash herdr plugin install persiyanov/herdr-reviewr ``` reviewr opens on its own when herdr creates a workspace for a worktree. To open it yourself: ```bash herdr plugin action invoke open --plugin persiyanov.reviewr ``` **To update**, reinstall. Your config stays: ```bash herdr plugin uninstall persiyanov.reviewr && herdr plugin install persiyanov/herdr-reviewr ``` **Without herdr**, run a [release binary](https://github.com/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr/releases/latest) on any repo. Everything but **Send** and the **last turn** scope works: ```bash herdr-reviewr ~/some/repo ``` ## Quick start 1. **Pick a file.** `j` / `k` in the file list, or `]` to jump from change to change. 2. **Focus the diff.** `Tab`. 3. **Select lines.** `v`, then `j` / `k`, or drag the line numbers. 4. **Comment.** `c`, type, `Enter`. 5. **Send.** `s` puts every comment in the agent's input: the only agent, or the one beside reviewr. `S` lets you pick. The footer shows the next step, and the worktree you're on at its right. `?` lists every key. To toggle reviewr with a key, add this to `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`: ```toml [[keys.command]] key = "cmd+r" # many macOS terminals swallow alt+ type = "plugin_action" command = "persiyanov.reviewr.toggle" ``` On Windows, `cmd` is the Windows key, and Windows takes `cmd+r` first. Use another key, such as `prefix+f`. A key for a remote machine goes in that machine's `config.toml`, because custom commands belong to the server where the panes run. Choose **reload config** in herdr's menu to apply it. ## Controls Every key can be rebound ([Keybindings](#keybindings)). **Getting around** | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `1` `2` `3` | Tab: Changes / All files / PR | | `u` `b` `t` `g` | Scope: uncommitted / branch / last turn / commits | | `B` | Pick the base branch | | `G` | Pick commits | | `W` | Switch to another worktree of this repo | | `j` `k` · `↑` `↓` | Move | | `]` `[` | Next / previous change | | `f` `F` | Next / previous file | | `PageUp` `PageDown` | Page | | `Ctrl+U` `Ctrl+D` | Half page | | `Tab` | Switch pane | | `→` `←` | Expand / collapse, or scroll sideways | | `/` | Search files and code | | `Ctrl+F` | Find in file | | `:` | Go to line (`:0` first, `:$` last) | | `w` | Wrap lines | | `m` | Rendered / source markdown | | `\|` | Unified / split diff (needs 137 columns) | | `p` | Move the file list | | `z` | Hide / show the file list | | `<` `>` | Widen / narrow the file list | | `r` | Refresh | | `?` | All keys | | `q` | Quit (asks if comments are unsent) | | `Q` | Quit and drop unsent comments | **Reviewing** | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `v` | Select lines | | `c` | Comment | | `e` | Edit the comment, or open the file in your editor | | `d` | Delete comment | | `n` `N` | Next / previous comment | | `l` | List comments | | `s` | Send comments to the agent beside reviewr, or pick one | | `S` | Pick the agent, then send | | `y` | Copy comments | | `esc` | Clear selection | **Comment box** | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `Enter` | Save | | `Esc` | Cancel | | `Shift+Enter` · `Alt+Enter` · `Ctrl+J` | New line | The usual editing keys work: arrows, `Home` / `End`, `Ctrl+A` / `Ctrl+E`, `Alt+b` / `Alt+f`, `Ctrl+W` / `Ctrl+U` / `Ctrl+K`. **PR tab** | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `j` `k` | Move through description and comments | | `PageUp` `PageDown` | Scroll | | `o` | Open in browser | | `r` | Refresh | **Mouse:** drag to copy, double-click a word, triple-click a line. Click or drag line numbers to comment. Click files, tabs, and links. Scroll with the wheel. ## The three tabs - **Changes** — files the current scope changed. - **All files** — every file in the worktree. You can comment here too. Git-ignored files are dimmed. - **PR** — the branch's pull request (merge request on GitLab): state, checks, description, comments. Switching between **Changes** and **All files** keeps your file and line when the other tab lists the file. `follow_file_across_tabs = false` gives each tab its own place instead. ## Diff scopes - **uncommitted** — changes since the last commit, including new files. - **branch** — everything since the branch left its base, commits included. The base is the default branch until you pick another ([Base branch](#base-branch)). - **last turn** — changes since the agent's latest turn started. - **commits** — one commit or a range, picked with `G`. reviewr starts in **uncommitted** (`default_scope` changes that). Git-ignored files never show in **Changes**. ## Configuration Flags on the pane command: | Flag | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `--base ` | auto | base for the branch scope, overrides the pick | | `--theme ` | `catppuccin` | color theme | | `--wrap ` | `on` | wrap long lines | Everything else goes in `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/persiyanov.reviewr/config.toml`. Saving it applies at once. An invalid file blocks the pane with the error until you fix it. ```toml theme = "tokyo-night" default_scope = "branch" # uncommitted | branch | last-turn markdown_view = "rendered" # source | rendered diff_view = "split" # unified | split navigator_position = "bottom" # right | bottom | left | top toggle_placement = "overlay" # split | overlay | zoomed | tab toggle_direction = "down" # right | down, for split auto_open = false follow_file_across_tabs = false scrolloff = 0 # lines kept around the diff cursor, 3 by default; 999 centers editor = "code -g {file}:{line}" url_opener = "browser-bridge --new-tab {url}" review_prefix = "Fix each comment, then run the tests." github_host = "github.example.com" gitlab_host = "git.corp.example" azure_devops_host = "tfs.corp.example" [keybindings] comment = ["c", "ㅊ"] ``` ### Theme Dark: `catppuccin`, `catppuccin-frappe`, `catppuccin-macchiato`, `dracula`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `one-dark`, `solarized`, `monokai`, `tokyo-night`, `rose-pine`, `ayu`, `everforest`. Light: `catppuccin-latte`, `gruvbox-light`, `one-light`, `solarized-light`, `github-light`, `tokyo-night-day`, `rose-pine-dawn`. Pick one that matches your terminal's background. Shared names match herdr's colors. ### Markdown and diff view `m` and `|` stick for every file you open until you press them again. `markdown_view` and `diff_view` set how a new pane starts. Split needs a diff pane 137 columns wide: hide the file list (`z`), move it below (`p`), or open reviewr zoomed or as an overlay. A narrower pane shows unified until it widens. ### File list `navigator_position` or `p` moves it. `<` / `>` or dragging its edge resizes it. `z` hides it. ### Base branch The branch scope compares against the repo's default branch. To pick another, press `B` or click the base name in the header. Type to filter, or type any commit reference like `HEAD~2`. The pick holds for this worktree until you change it. `--base` overrides it. ### Editor `e` opens the file at your line in `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR`, or git's `core.editor`. Common editors open at the right line. A terminal editor takes the pane until you quit. For anything else, set `editor`; `{file}` and `{line}` are filled in. ### URL opener Links open with `open`, `xdg-open`, or the Windows default browser. Under `herdr --remote`, set `url_opener` to something that reaches your browser. The URL is passed as one argument, never through a shell, so don't use `ssh host open {url}`. ### Review prefix `review_prefix` goes above your comments on every send and copy. It arrives as pasted text, so Claude Code won't run a `/command` in it. To run one, type it in the agent's input before you press `s`. ### Keybindings Each action takes a list of keys that replaces its defaults. The footer shows the first. Extra keys help non-Latin layouts: bind the character your layout types on the same key. | Action | Default | | --- | --- | | `down` / `up` | `j` / `k` | | `next-hunk` / `prev-hunk` | `]` / `[` | | `next-file` / `prev-file` | `f` / `F` | | `switch-pane` | `tab` | | `scope-uncommitted` / `scope-branch` / `scope-last-turn` / `scope-commits` | `u` / `b` / `t` / `g` | | `base-pick` / `commit-pick` | `B` / `G` | | `worktree-pick` | `W` | | `tab-changes` / `tab-all-files` / `tab-pr` | `1` / `2` / `3` | | `wrap` | `w` | | `rendered` | `m` | | `split` | `\|` | | `navigator-position` | `p` | | `navigator-hide` | `z` | | `navigator-grow` / `navigator-shrink` | `<` / `>` | | `select` | `v` | | `comment` | `c` | | `edit` / `delete` | `e` / `d` | | `next-comment` / `prev-comment` | `n` / `N` | | `comments` | `l` | | `search` | `/` | | `find` | `ctrl+f` | | `goto-line` | `:` | | `keys` | `?` | | `send` | `s` | | `send-to` | `S` | | `copy` | `y`, `Y` | | `open-pr` | `o` | | `refresh` | `r` | | `quit` | `q` | | `quit-discard` | `Q` | A key is one character, a named key (`tab`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, `pageup`, `pagedown`), or a `ctrl+` / `alt+` chord. `Esc` and `Enter` are fixed. ### GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps The PR tab reads the `upstream` remote, else `origin`, so forks work. Self-hosted servers need `github_host`, `gitlab_host`, or `azure_devops_host`, matching the remote's hostname exactly. An SSH alias like `github.com-work` resolves through your ssh config to the host it stands for. ### Pane placement The toggle opens reviewr right of your agent. `toggle_placement` changes that: `overlay` covers the tab, `zoomed` fills it, `tab` opens a new one. Each tab gets its own reviewr; with `tab` placement, each worktree gets its own reviewr tab. The toggle closes your reviewr when you can see it, takes you to it when you can't, and opens one when there's none. `close` closes yours. reviewr opens on its own in a new worktree's workspace, with `split` or `tab` only, and leaves your agent focused. `auto_open = false` turns that off. ### Layouts To place reviewr in a herdr layout, give a pane `command = "herdr-reviewr"`. If `~/.local/bin` isn't on your `PATH`, use `~/.local/state/herdr/plugins/persiyanov.reviewr/bin/herdr-reviewr`. On Windows, point it at the plugin's own `bin` folder. ## Limitations - **Colors need a 24-bit terminal**, and the theme must be matched to the background by hand. - **Added and removed lines differ only by color.** - **Copying** needs `pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, `xclip`, or `xsel` (Windows needs none). Send works without. - **Windows:** a reviewr started by hand in a PowerShell pane isn't recognized, so toggle opens another. Toggle may open on the pane's launch folder, not where you `cd`'d. - **Network drives send no file events.** macOS and Linux check every five seconds. On Windows, press `r`. - **Send needs an agent in the workspace**, and refuses one at a permission prompt. Your comments stay. With several agents, it goes to the only one in reviewr's tab, else it asks. - **last turn shows all of a turn or nothing.** If the agent writes the instant a turn starts, the scope shows nothing for that turn and says why. - **The PR tab** supports GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps only. A merged or closed PR shows as history. Each comment list shows its newest 100. - **A background pane** catches up 30 seconds after a change, or at once when shown. - **A rename can pair with the wrong file** until you press `r`. - **Comments live only in the pane.** Closing it loses unsent ones. Send delivers all or none. - **Comments don't follow moved code.** reviewr marks them stale instead of dropping them. - **Files over 2 MB or 50,000 lines** aren't diffed. Neither are binary files. ## Building from source See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To run your build in herdr: ```bash git clone https://github.com/persiyanov/herdr-reviewr cd herdr-reviewr just install # build to bin/herdr-reviewr, re-signed on macOS herdr plugin uninstall persiyanov.reviewr herdr plugin link . ``` Toggle the pane off and on after every `just install`. ## Roadmap JSON export, marking files reviewed, more named keys, automatic light/dark theme, more themes (`kanagawa`, `vesper`, a dark `github`), a theme that follows the terminal, copying through the terminal. ## Sponsors reviewr is built by one person. If it saves you time, [sponsor it](https://github.com/sponsors/persiyanov). Company sponsors get their logo here. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Syntax highlighting by [syntect](https://github.com/trishume/syntect) and [two-face](https://github.com/CosmicHorrorDev/two-face), whose bundled themes color most syntax. Bundled syntax themes in `assets/`, each under its own license: - [Catppuccin Mocha](https://github.com/catppuccin/bat) — MIT. - [Tokyo Night](https://github.com/folke/tokyonight.nvim) (`tokyo-night`, `tokyo-night-day`) — Apache-2.0. - [Rosé Pine](https://github.com/rose-pine/tm-theme) (`rose-pine`, `rose-pine-dawn`) — MIT. - [ayu](https://github.com/dempfi/ayu) (`ayu`) — MIT, converted from its Sublime color scheme. - [Everforest](https://github.com/sainnhe/everforest) (`everforest`) — MIT, built from its palette and highlight groups.
